title: Large low-degree Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ have variance at least $1/2$ when viewed as a real-valued function on the sign cube. Write $d$ for its Friedgut degree at parameter $1/8$ and $J$ for its Friedgut coordinate set at that parameter. Then some nonempty set $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ satisfies $|S|\le d$ and $\frac{1}{4(d+1)(|J|+1)^d}\le \widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of the real-valued form of $f$ at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The variance of the real-valued form of $f$ is at least $1/2$
replaced:
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function whose real-valued form has variance
at least $1/2$. Then there is a nonempty coordinate set $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
with $|S|\leq d$, where $d$ is the Friedgut degree of $f$ at parameter $1/8$, such that
$\frac{1}{4(d+1)(|J|+1)^d}\leq\widehat{f}(S)^2$. Here $J$ is the Friedgut coordinate set
of $f$ at parameter $1/8$, and $\widehat{f}(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of the
real-valued form of $f$.
